C11 and C12 use similar presidential-approval machinery, but their designated actors and broader formulations are less closely matched.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The authority vested in the heads of departments and agencies ... may be exercised by such heads of departments and agencies without the approval of the President.","parent_excerpt":"The heads of the several departments and agencies of the Government are hereby authorized and empowered, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President, to exercise ... the authority conferred upon the President","explanation":"Both provisions center on department and agency heads exercising specified statutory authority without further presidential approval."},{"child_excerpt":"by subsection (b) of section 16 of the Federal Airport Act ... to perform any acts and to execute any instruments necessary","parent_excerpt":"by section 202 (c) (2) of the Annual and Sick Leave Act of 1951 ... to authorize leaves of absence","explanation":"Each adapts the same compact statutory-authority formula to a different substantive power."}]}
